column1: # iota(4,11) >= 32 ?  one line per deg(0) cube of the symmetry-broken encoding.
# Written by tools/rung.sh; each line is one `iota_sym --only-deg` invocation.
# The rung is UNSAT only when EVERY cube is UNSAT. A cube marked
# `undecided` carries the budget it was stopped at, per docs/reading.md rule 13.
# SIX OF THESE CUBES ARE PROVABLY EMPTY AND DID NOT NEED SOLVING.
# In a 4-uniform sunflower-free family every point has degree at most
# g(3): the star at a point IS its link, which is 3-uniform, distinct and
# sunflower-free (PureLink.link_at_point_bounded).  PureLink.g_three_at_most_26
# gives g(3) <= 26 unconditionally, so deg(0) >= 27 is impossible and
# cubes 27..32 contain nothing.  They were solved anyway, before this was
# noticed, and cadical returned UNSAT for every one -- which is a cross
# check of the encoding against the kernel rather than wasted work, but
# it was not deliberate.
# With AbbottGardner1969 (g(3) = 20) the empty range widens to 21..32 and
# only deg(0) = 12..20 can hold anything.  That value is a citation, so
# the unconditional statement is the one this file is run against.
# Cube 12 -- the floor, and the one 33.5a expected to be worst -- was
# decided on an Apple M4 Air, not on the session container: RUNG_THREADS=8
# RUNG_SLICE=900, so it stalled at 900 s, split into 19 degree-sequence
# sub-cubes and finished UNSAT at 3236.4 s with none at the limit. That
# is 33.5a's "nineteen sequences" for deficiency four, confirmed. Every
# other row was measured on the container.
# deg0
